01 · The list

Question words,
level by level

The question words of Japanese: what, who, where, when, why, how, which, how many and how much, from the JLPT vocabulary lists with readings and meanings. Learn these first and you can ask for everything else.

In Lock&Learn Japanese these words sit in their level packs (JLPT N5, JLPT N3, JLPT N1), one per glance on the widget: a word waits in kanji, the way the test shows it; one tap reveals the reading, the meaning and a real sentence. JLPT N5 is free; every other pack opens with a free preview and another word unlocks daily.

Type to filter by word, reading or meaning. Flashcards hides the reading and the meaning until you tap a row; Shuffle deals the list in a new order.

03 · Questions

Asked and
answered

What are the question words in Japanese?

The table lists the 20 interrogatives on the JLPT vocabulary lists with their readings and meanings, each beginner-level one with a real sentence that shows where it sits in the question.

Which JLPT levels are these words from?

17 from JLPT N5, 2 from JLPT N3, 1 from JLPT N1. The level chip on each row says where the word sits, so you can stop at your level or read ahead. Beginner-level words carry a real example sentence; the rest show word, reading and meaning, with their sentences in the app.

How do I learn question words words on my iPhone Lock Screen?

Install Lock&Learn Japanese, then touch and hold your Lock Screen, tap Customize, tap the widget area and choose Lock&Learn Japanese. Enable the level packs these words come from (JLPT N5, JLPT N3, JLPT N1). A word waits in kanji, the way the test shows it; one tap reveals the reading, the meaning and a real sentence.

Is Lock&Learn Japanese free?

Yes. The app is free on iOS: JLPT N5 is free, every other pack opens with a free preview, and another word unlocks daily. Lock&Learn+ is an optional upgrade that opens every pack at once, offered as a yearly plan or a one-time lifetime purchase.
